current_state_evidence.symbol: captured turn metadata for the failed weather request
current_state_evidence.observation: The captured run records interpreter_status=unavailable after a 502 response, a fallback contract with conversation plus tool_discovery and mutation forbidden, activation_allowed_tool_names containing only tool_search, deferred tool_result_read, and capability_not_required exclusions for web_search, web_fetch, and get_current_time.

ConversationResolution carries contract, task state, bounded context, and diagnostics but has no typed interpreter-versus-fallback provenance; resolve selects _fallback_resolution whenever no validated contract exists.

The deterministic fallback intentionally grants only conversation and tool_discovery, forbids mutation, and sets confidence to zero; this permits pure conversation but provides no safe lookup activation envelope.

The rollout converts the policy-eligible BaseTool catalog into descriptors and calls CapabilityPlanner.plan with only the resolved contract and policy/environment ceilings, so structured fallback provenance is currently lost at this boundary.

Eligibility requires a tool capability to intersect required_capabilities. Under fallback, required_capabilities is tool_discovery, so safe web and time tools are excluded as capability_not_required; exposed_tools is then selected as a minimal cover of the available required capabilities.

The existing descriptor already centralizes capabilities, read_only, destructive, requires_approval, risk, and directly_exposable metadata, which is sufficient to define a general policy predicate without request keywords or tool-name lists.

The activation allowlist is derived from capability_plan.eligible_tools, but discoverability separately admits neutral infrastructure tools. This permits tool_result_read to be deferred even when it is absent from activation_allowed_tool_names.

current_state_evidence.symbol: AgentEngine._invoke_shared_runtime activation policy and registry view construction
current_state_evidence.observation: The engine copies adapter activation_allowed_tool_names into ToolExecutionContext and passes exposure tool_names plus discoverable_tool_names into ToolRegistry.create_view, making the adapter output the real producer consumed by runtime activation.

create_view adds tool_activate whenever discoverable names contain a deferred tool, while request_tool_activation denies a deferred tool unless it appears in activation_allowed_tool_names. Therefore discoverability and authorization must be consistent before view creation.
update_plan is state-changing and reports is_read_only false; engine and react-loop logic expose it only when the durable plan runtime is explicitly active, so semantic fallback must not grant it.
The existing outage regression proves only that a no-tool answer can complete; it does not exercise discovery, activation, invocation, or denial through the real engine-to-registry boundary.

If the source cannot be assigned from control flow, stop; do not infer it from diagnostics text, confidence, objective content, exception text, or user phrasing.

When semantic fallback is active, keep required_capabilities unchanged and augment only eligible_tools with catalog entries satisfying the centralized safe read-only capability predicate; compute exposed_tools only as the minimal cover of contract-required capabilities.

control_flow.kind: implementation phase 3: exposure and activation consistency
control_flow.failure_path: Derive activation allowlist, discoverable tools, and effective deferred tools from the same policy-filtered eligible set; remove any bypass that creates a deferred tool outside the activation allowlist.
If adapter diagnostics and exposure discoverability disagree, fail the integration gate before constructing a registry view.
Create tool_activate only when the effective deferred set is nonempty and every deferred tool is activation-authorized.

Policy-ineligible, unsafe, denied, non-discoverable, or plan-runtime-only tools remain denied; an authorized safe read-only tool is atomically activated and made callable for the next model iteration.

invariants.statement: Every ConversationResolution states whether its authoritative contract came from an accepted interpreter result or the deterministic fallback, and downstream code consumes that typed state instead of reverse-engineering diagnostics.
invariants.prohibited_behavior: Inferring fallback from confidence==0, an empty objective, evidence text, interpreter_status strings, exception messages, or request content.
invariants.counterexample: A valid interpreter result with low confidence or an empty objective is mislabeled as fallback and gains the fallback activation envelope.
phase_exit: Accepted, unavailable, rejected, and absent interpreter paths assign the expected source.
No diagnostic or natural-language parser is used as the source of truth.

invariants.statement: During semantic fallback, eligible_tools may be augmented only by policy-eligible catalog tools that are read-only, low risk, non-destructive, require no approval, contain neither workspace_write nor execution, and match a centralized safe capability contract: temporal_lookup, open_world_lookup, literature_research, workspace_read, or tool_discovery.
invariants.prohibited_behavior: Admitting a tool because its name, description, user request, city, weather phrase, language, provider, or current bug example matches a literal list.
invariants.counterexample: A tool named safe_weather_lookup that requires approval or also carries execution is admitted merely because the request asks for weather.
phase_exit: Safe candidates are selected solely from normalized CatalogToolDescriptor metadata and existing policy ceilings.
Different languages and unrelated lookup phrasing produce the same safe fallback envelope.

invariants.statement: Semantic fallback does not add lookup candidates to required_capabilities or direct exposure; required_capabilities remains tool_discovery and exposed_tools remains the minimal cover of contract-required capabilities, normally tool_search.
invariants.enforcement_owner: CapabilityPlanner.plan separation of eligible_tools from _minimal_exposure inputs
invariants.prohibited_behavior: Changing fallback operations to open_world_lookup or passing fallback activation-only capabilities into the direct schema cover.
invariants.counterexample: An interpreter outage causes every safe web, literature, time, and workspace-read schema to be sent directly to the model on the first iteration.
phase_exit: Lookup tools are activatable but not directly exposed before activation.

invariants.statement: For every enforced exposure plan, effective deferred_tools is a subset of activation_allowed_tool_names after all hard ceilings and schema-budget reconciliation.
invariants.enforcement_owner: capability_exposure_adapter.adapt_capability_plan_to_exposure derivation of discoverable and deferred tool names
invariants.prohibited_behavior: Adding neutral infrastructure or baseline discoverable tools after the activation allowlist has been computed.
invariants.counterexample: tool_result_read appears in deferred_tool_names while activation_allowed_tool_names contains only tool_search, causing a broker that can never authorize its only deferred tool.
phase_exit: The adapter asserts or constructs the subset relation after final reconciliation.
The engine-to-registry integration fixture observes the same set on both sides.

invariants.statement: The activation broker is present if and only if at least one genuinely activatable deferred tool remains, and its reserved schema slot is included in the runtime schema budget.
invariants.enforcement_owner: capability_exposure_adapter broker_required calculation and ToolRegistry.create_view deferred-name check
invariants.prohibited_behavior: Creating tool_activate for an empty or entirely unauthorized deferred set, or exceeding the schema limit after broker insertion.
invariants.counterexample: The only discoverable item is an unauthorized tool_result_read, yet tool_activate is inserted and consumes a schema slot.
phase_exit: Zero effective deferred tools yields no broker.
One or more authorized deferred tools yields exactly one broker without exceeding the schema limit.

invariants.statement: Interpreter fallback never expands mutation, execution, destructive, approval-required, denied, sandbox-ineligible, or durable plan-runtime authority; update_plan remains unavailable unless the existing plan runtime explicitly exposes it.
invariants.enforcement_owner: CapabilityPlanner.plan policy predicate, ExposurePolicyCeilings, and ToolRegistry.request_tool_activation
invariants.prohibited_behavior: Treating all non-destructive or all read-looking tools as safe without checking read_only, risk, approval, capabilities, allowlist, denylist, sandbox, and plan-runtime ownership.
invariants.counterexample: After a 502 interpretation failure, the model activates update_plan, exec_command, file_write, a destructive read tool, or an approval-required network tool.
phase_exit: Positive safe lookup activation and negative unsafe activation are exercised through the real registry view.
Existing explicit update_plan exposure tests continue to pass.

invariants.statement: When semantic interpretation succeeds, required capabilities, eligible tools, direct exposure, mutation handling, and activation behavior remain unchanged from the existing contract-driven path.
invariants.enforcement_owner: ConversationResolver.resolve source branch and CapabilityPlanner.plan semantic_fallback=false branch
invariants.prohibited_behavior: Applying the broad safe fallback envelope to accepted interpreter results or weakening their operation-specific minimal exposure.
invariants.counterexample: A successfully interpreted temporal_lookup request gains workspace_read and literature tools as activation candidates, or a successful weather request changes its direct web subset.
phase_exit: Existing successful weather, temporal lookup, write, clarification, allowlist, and denylist tests pass unchanged.

invariants.statement: Fallback behavior is independent of natural-language tokens and generalizes across languages, synonyms, locations, and lookup domains because it is determined only by resolution provenance, catalog metadata, capability contracts, and runtime policy.
invariants.enforcement_owner: ConversationResolver provenance and CapabilityPlanner catalog-policy abstraction
